documents.unit: Artificial Intelligence Policy Committee (A-State Knowledge Base)
documents.title: Guidelines and Considerations for the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: University-wide guidelines from the campus AI Policy Committee that leave the decision to faculty, offering four syllabus approaches from prohibited to freely permitted. They also explain how to use AI detectors (Turnitin, K-16) with caution and urge instructors to state expectations clearly.
documents.stance_why: The text says it was designed so 'faculty retain the authority to determine the scope of acceptable usage of AI in their courses' and lists four approaches (Use Prohibited, Use with Permission, Use with Acknowledgement, Use Freely Permitted) for instructors to choose; it sets no single stance, so delegates with tiers.

units.why: The guidelines say instructors set the scope of AI use in their courses, which is a statement of who decides, so P04; it informs rather than binds.
units.anchor: faculty retain the authority to determine the scope of acceptable usage of AI in their

units.why: Advises instructors to put an AI policy in the syllabus: 'Faculty are advised to include their AI policies in their syllabi'. That is the syllabus-statement type P09, with advisory (should) strength.
units.anchor: Faculty are advised to include their AI policies in their syllabi

units.why: States the institutional purpose: the university 'must maximize opportunities to benefit' from AI, a principle for the whole institution, so P56 framework; it leans toward embracing AI.
units.anchor: must maximize opportunities to benefit from these rapidly evolving technologies

units.why: Second half of the framework: the university 'must conscientiously address ethical considerations' for 'responsible and fair utilization', an institution-level principle (P56) rather than a specific ethics concern.
units.anchor: must conscientiously address ethical considerations to guarantee the responsible and fair utilization of these tools

units.why: Sets a principle that AI use be human-centered and 'enhance human intelligence and expertise rather than attempting to supplant them'. It is an institution-level principle (P56); P32 is about students as problem-solvers and this is not specific to students.
units.anchor: their use crafted to enhance human intelligence and expertise rather than attempting to supplant them

units.why: A listed human-centered practice: 'Gathering input from students, faculty, and various stakeholders' to adjust AI systems. It is a feedback mechanism, closest to P54 (feedback invited), though it concerns AI systems not the policy.
units.anchor: Gathering input from students, faculty, and various stakeholders

units.why: Lists as a practice 'upholding the independence of faculty' to decide AI integration; again decision rests with instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: upholding the independence of faculty and educational institutions in determining the integration of AI technologies

units.why: Colleges, departments and faculty are to be empowered to 'personalize and match requirements and policies regarding AI use' to their courses, so rules are set locally (P04).
units.anchor: personalize and match requirements and policies regarding AI use to their course and program outcomes

units.why: Says AI research and AI-assisted research are 'central' and supported; this concerns research use, so P62 rather than teaching types.

units.why: Places responsibility on 'each college, department, and individual faculty member' to open clear channels about generative AI; a duty to communicate expectations, P09.

units.why: Instructs units and faculty to weigh 'four basic approaches' (prohibited, permission, acknowledgement, freely permitted) when writing statements; named levels, P05.

units.why: Requires that syllabus or assignment statements 'fully explain the circumstances under which students may use generative AI'; communication in syllabus/assignments, P09.

units.why: If AI is restricted, it is 'crucial to engage in discussions with enrolled students' on scope and conditions; communicating expectations, P09.

units.why: Under 'Use Prohibited', faculty 'may entirely prohibit the use of AI' where students work independently. This is a ban option on all work in the course, P01, though only offered as an option.
units.anchor: faculty may entirely prohibit the use of AI

units.why: Instructors should clearly inform students of a ban and explain why; about communicating the rule, P09.

units.why: Under 'Use with Permission', AI may be allowed 'in specific instances or assignments but not in others'; decided per assignment, P04 (P05 names the tier set elsewhere).

units.why: Instructors should say 'when and how' students can use AI 'and how they can receive permission'; the instruction is to communicate, so P09.

units.why: Under 'Use with Acknowledgement', students may use AI 'throughout the course, provided they clearly cite or acknowledge their use'; a default permit with a condition, P02.

units.why: Requires specifying 'the type and format of citation or acknowledgment methods'; disclosure with each submission, P24 (P25 requires specific citation contents, which are not named).
units.anchor: explicitly specify the type and format of citation or acknowledgment methods students should employ

units.why: Under 'Use Freely Permitted', students may use AI 'without the explicit requirement to cite or acknowledge'; open permission, P02.

units.why: Even under free use students must 'grasp the boundaries, risks, and ethical applications' of the tools. This fits no type exactly (P31 is about verifying output), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: it remains critical for students in such circumstances to grasp the boundaries, risks, and ethical
units.uncovered_note: Students must understand the boundaries, risks and ethical applications of AI tools even when use is freely permitted.
